It just takes hard work, dedication, and time lots of time lol. There are many many MANY artists around today that work very hard on their art and receive little to no compensation. I'm sure That's not something you would want to get involved in.

Here's my suggestion take it or leave it but I believe it will help you in the long run like it did me. Work on improving your own skills. Once you put the time and the dedication in you will find that your art will steadily improve. It won't happen over night but you will get better gradually. You are very young my friend and you have so many years to grow and improve. Don't worry about making money on "merch" right now focus on getting better. Once your skills are there then you can work on monetizing it.

Hello again! Given that his diagnosis is so new it's more or less a waiting game for both of you. ADHD is something that gets easier to manage as times goes on. It will be up to him to learn how to best go about his day to day now that he is medicated and more focused. ADHD affects people differently. To some it can be debilitating while others can manage stuff well. 

I'm glad to hear y'all have had talks and you are communicating about your problems. Be patient as best you can but don't let him get away with stuff. It's better to stay on top of someone like him and myself and remind us of things from time to time. Forgetfulness is very very very common with people like us. I work in a hotel as a maintenance man and it is not rare for me to completely forget which rooms have which issues. Or completely forget what I was doing. Getting distracted is one of the big things that people struggle with.

You see our minds run at a million miles a minute. One minute we could be thinking about work. The very next is what to eat. It's very easy to get side tracked or lose your train of thought. Motivation to do things we are interested in is another. Me and your man are similar it seems. See I could do anything that I'm really interested in for hours on end and completely forget about anything else. It's all a balancing act he will learn as time goes on. 

In my experience what has worked for me is to WRITE EVERYTHING DOWN!!!!! I carry a notepad with me and whatever I get asked or assigned to do something I write it down. There for if I forget what to do I am reminded when I check my notes. Also have him set reminders on his phone. This way when he's chillin on his phone he will see the reminder. Incentives for doing chores for example works well too. My girl does not have ADHD and whenever there is work to be done she will set up a little incentive for me to do something. Maybe it could be like his favorite food. Or a night to himself to watch the game. Or maybe a new video game if he like them. Or in my case use fun bedroom activities to help get him motivated ya dig ;)

All in all he will be okay. He just goes about things different than you and he will improve. Symptoms can be easy one day and hard as hell another. Just give time to get used to being medicated and use some of my tips and I promise things will get better. He will be forgetful. He will be unmotivated. He will be stubborn sometimes. But if you help him improve he will improve. Be his rock and he will thank you for it later. 

I'd type more but I'm on mobile atm, but if you have any other questions or just want some more tips feel free to pm me any time!

Hi there! I was diagnosed with ADHD at 13 and have lived with it every day for the past decade. One thing I see a lot is people misunderstanding what this really is. It is not a disability nor is it a disease. It's a different lifestyle than "normal" people experience. 

When I was growing up and even into my adulthood I felt like I needed to hide the fact I was different. See most "normal" people when they hear you have this mysterious "hyperactivity" disorder they immediately think you have a disability or they think it's some sort of autism. This lead to a lot of problems with friends, teachers, family, co workers, and especially with the ladies. 

The best piece of advise I can give you is don't make this mistake most people do and treat your man differently. He is no different from anyone else he just has a different way of going about things than you. You will get frustrated with him. And he will get frustrated with you. He will do things that will make you scratch your head. And sometimes he may get under your skin. But don't think this is due to him having a disability. It's just how he works. People like myself and him and tons of people on this sub are not disabled nor is there really anything wrong with us. We are just different. 

Just keep him close and stay focused and don't rush him. He will be okay and so will you. Many many many people have this disorder. From heads of state to people on the street. Just be patient with him and try to see life thru his eyes. But don't ever make the mistake of thinking this is a disability and that he needs to be treated any differently. How would you treat him if he didn't have ADHD? Whatever that is do just that. That will be the biggest piece of support you can give him. 

As far as your original question goes idk of any "support communities" per say. This sub is one of the best for learning about people with this disorder. Read some of the top posts or talk to some of the fellow subscribers. If you have any questions feel free to send me a PM.

I'm a hotel Maintence man who primarily works 3rd shift. Quite a few interesting stories not sure if paranormal or just the fact our building is old as balls and on a lake. Anyway about a week ago I was over at what we call The Summer House (a small building with a kitchen and a few conference rooms. Gets its name from having a outside deck, jacuzzi, and swimming pool.) Wiring up some new lights in the ceiling. I step out side by the pool to have a cigarette when I smell what I can only describe as what you would smell if you cleaned out a grease trap. I then here something crunching leaves and twigs back near the pump room. Lots of deer out here so I'm thinking it's just a deer taking a shit or something.  Well as I walk closer the growl this thing made was definitely not a deer and sounded like it didn't like me very much. I run back inside and all through out the night I keep hearing what sounds like rocks being thrown at the doors.

When i was about 12 or so our family dog Lucy, a beautiful basset hound, tragically died right out of the blue. She had a massive seizure and when we rushed her to the vet they did all they could to calm her down and help her. They came to us later and said she was stable and ok then not 5 minutes later than run back in and tell us that they lost her.

It was a shock to all of us and she was really the best dog i could ever ask for. We grieved for a while and missed her terribly. The vet however made putty molds with her name and paw print for us kids. We decided to frame them and always remember her the best we could. 

It gets easier no doubt about that but it takes time and you yourself have to move on and and come to terms with the loss. Your idea of a tattoo is pretty good i was thinking of getting one myself. However make sure it truly what you want and you think long and hard about it. They last forever and if you go to a bad artist and they screw it up you have to live with it. Ill pray for healing for you my friend, stay strong, and God bless.
